title: Revisiting the Dragonfly galaxy - I. High-resolution ALMA and VLA observations of the radio hotspots in a hyper-luminous infrared galaxy at z = 1.92
question: Investigate the radio properties, structure, evolution stage, lifetime of hotspots, and geometry of radio jets of the Dragonfly galaxy (MRC 0152-209) at z = 1.92 using high-resolution ALMA 237 GHz and VLA 44 GHz continuum observations.

what.value: Total flux densities at 74 MHz (3100 +/- 620 mJy), 365 MHz (1580 +/- 30 mJy), and 1.4 GHz (453 +/- 91 mJy)
Total flux density at 147 MHz (2620 +/- 10 mJy)

evidence.quote: Column (8): references to flux measurements. 1: (cite: 2010AA...511A..53V); 2: (cite: 2018MNRAS.474.5008D); 3: (cite: 2000AAS..145..121P); 4: this work.

what.value: VLA 4.7 GHz and 8.2 GHz flux densities for Total, NW, and SE components, and equipartition magnetic field limit B_eq = 160 uG

evidence.quote: However, in the SE hotspot, adopting a lower limit of the magnetic field in energy equipartition $B\mathrm{_{eq}}$, (cite: 2000AAS..145..121P) gives $B\mathrm{_{eq}}=160\ \mu$G, which is much higher than the expected $B_\mathrm{CMB}$ (see §[\[sec:fitting\]](#sec:fitting)).

what.value: ATCA continuum total flux density at 40 GHz (S_nu = 5.1 +/- 1.5 mJy)

evidence.quote: This is supported by the low-resolution Australia Telescope Compact Array continuum observation at 40 GHz that has a total flux density $S_\nu=5.1\pm1.5$ mJy (cite: 2011ApJ...734L..25E)

what.value: Star formation rate (~3000 M_sun yr^-1) and stellar mass (~5x10^11 M_sun) of the Dragonfly galaxy, and Giant Molecular Cloud (Companion) offset

evidence.quote: In this work, we have studied a HzRG – MRC 0152-209, named Dragonfly galaxy, which has a star formation rate (SFR) of $\mathrm{\sim3000\ M_\odot\ yr^{-1}}$ and $M_\star\sim\mathrm{5\times10^{11}\ M_\odot}$ (cite: 2015A&A...584A..99E; 2015MNRAS.451.1025E).
Furthermore, (cite: 2015A&A...584A..99E) has found a giant molecular cloud lying close to the propagation direction of the SE jet, offset from the jet propagation axis by $\sim0.3\ensuremath{''}$

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image VLA 44 GHz and ALMA 237 GHz continuum data and align images
recipe.method: Calibrate raw data using CASA pipelines, flag CO(6-5) line and atmospheric absorption channels in ALMA data, compute dirty image RMS, clean down to 3 sigma using hogbom and Briggs robust +0.5 in tclean, and overlay contours in CARTA (shifting VLA 8.2 GHz WCS to match the VLA 44 GHz SE peak pixel).
key_parameters: robustness parameter +0.5; clean stop threshold 3 sigma; hogbom deconvolver

recipe.goal: Measure component flux densities, deconvolved hotspot size, spectral indices, and radio luminosities/powers
recipe.method: Integrate flux densities over specified apertures for NW, SE, and Core components, fit a single Gaussian component to the image plane to measure the deconvolved size of the SE hotspot, and calculate spectral indices, spectral luminosities, and radio powers.
key_parameters: Apertures: 0.4'' x 0.2'' (NW at 44 GHz), 0.5'' x 0.4'' (SE at 44 GHz), 0.07'' x 0.12'' (SE at 237 GHz), 0.4'' x 0.3'' (Core at 44 GHz)
assumptions: At 4.7 and 8.2 GHz, peak flux densities equal integrated flux densities (S_peak = S_total); at 237 GHz, SE sub-component is dominated by AGN synchrotron radiation; 3 sigma upper limit assumed for NW at 237 GHz.

recipe.goal: Fit low-frequency curved SED and classify as Compact-Steep-Spectrum (CSS) source
recipe.method: Fit observed total flux densities at <= 8.2 GHz with a curved power-law model S_nu = a * nu^alpha * exp(q * (ln nu)^2) and compare the derived turnover frequency with the empirical size-turnover frequency relation for CSS sources.
key_parameters: Frequencies <= 8.2 GHz; projected linear size l ~ 13 kpc
assumptions: Observations at <= 1.4 GHz represent the sum of all three components (core, SE, NW)

recipe.goal: Fit synchrotron ageing models and derive equipartition magnetic fields and synchrotron ages
recipe.method: Fit the radio SEDs of NW and SE hotspots (>= 147 MHz) using SYNCHROFIT with continuous injection (CI), JP, and KP models to obtain break frequency nu_br, injection index s (alpha_inj = (1-s)/2), and remnant fraction T; compute equipartition magnetic field B_eq and synchrotron age t_s.
key_parameters: Frequencies >= 147 MHz; proton-to-electron energy ratio k = 1; Doppler boosting factor delta = 2-4; B_CMB = 3.25(1+z)^2 uG
assumptions: Unresolved flux densities at <= 1.4 GHz emanate only from NW and SE hotspots with flux ratio S_SE : S_NW = 15 : 1; hotspot occupies an elliptical cylinder volume.

recipe.goal: Estimate jet advance speed, Doppler boosting factor, jet kinetic power, and potential molecular outflow mass
recipe.method: Use the SE-to-NW flux density ratio R = ((1 + beta cos(theta))/(1 - beta cos(theta)))^(3 - alpha) to constrain the jet advance speed beta and Doppler factor delta; derive intrinsic 1.4 GHz radio power, compute jet kinetic power P_jet via empirical correlation, and estimate outflow mass M_out from energy conservation.
key_parameters: Flux ratios R ~ 15 (at 4.7 and 8.2 GHz) and R ~ 6 (at 44 and 237 GHz); outflow velocity ~1000 km s^-1
assumptions: SE hotspot contributes ~90% of total observed 1.4 GHz flux density and is Doppler boosted by factor delta = 2

answer_key.quantity: Projected linear separation between SE and NW hotspots

evidence.quote: The projected linear distance between the two hotspots is $\sim13$ kpc, yielding a linear size ($\leq20$ kpc) of a Compact-Steep-Spectrum (CSS) source.
Since the projected linear separation of the two hotspots is only $\sim1.5\ensuremath{''}$ ($\sim13$ kpc at $z=1.92$), the Dragonfly galaxy can be classified as a CSS source

answer_key.quantity: Advance speed of jet head (beta)

evidence.quote: In this scenario, we estimate the advance speed of the jet head, ranging from $\sim$0.1c – 0.3c, which yields a mildly relativistic case.
we find two ranges for $\beta$: $\sim0.2$c$-0.3$c for $R\sim15$ and $\sim0.1$c$-0.2$c for $R\sim6$.

answer_key.quantity: Approaching jet total kinetic power (P_jet)

evidence.quote: Adopting an empirical correlation between the radio power at 1.4 GHz and the kinetic power of the jet $P_\mathrm{jet}$ (cite: 2010ApJ...720.1066C), the approaching jet associated with the SE hotspot has a total jet kinetic power $P\mathrm{_{jet}=(7\pm9)\times10^{46}\ erg\ s^{-1}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Potential jet-driven molecular gas outflow mass (M_out)

evidence.quote: Even taking a lower limit on the SE jet lifetime, the total energy injection is $E\sim1\times10^{59}$ erg, suggesting that the jet kinetic energy can result in a significant molecular gas outflow of $M_\mathrm{out}\sim7\times10^9 \ \mathrm{M_\odot}$

score_reason: Public archival data, explicit CASA and pipeline versions, standard non-interactive tclean settings (hogbom, Briggs robust 0.5, 3-sigma threshold), complete flux table (Table 2), and public SED-fitting software (SYNCHROFIT), with only minor imaging/aperture geometry parameters omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA and VLA raw datasets are public, the calibration and continuum imaging follow a straightforward pipeline + standard tclean recipe without self-calibration, and the main results are quantitative flux densities, spectral indices, and SYNCHROFIT parameters.
